facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 金_七杀 (Metal carrying The General). Persona The General (七杀). Definition line: "Pressure that doesn't grant permission, the trial that forges". Keyword Force, charge fierce, poles catalyst Command / friction Harshness. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: pressure that does not ask permission; peace can feel like demotion. Arena: forge, campaign, the weight of command, tempering. Classical portrait: pressure as clarity; the trial that forges; force without permission; peace felt as demotion. Ruled domains: Pressure, Command, Crisis. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正官.
Element arena: Metal (edge, blade, ore, forge, whetstone, the clean line). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Wood. structural_interaction seed: "Metal pressing Wood same-polarity — the cutting force that doesn't grant permission".
- k2_overview: "Your Metal moves as the General: edge given rank. Pressure organizes you, crisis promotes you, and your will cuts through what committees cannot. This is the sword in its born office, decisive, disciplined, feared a little and needed often. Command the campaigns worth blood. Sheathe everywhere else."
- k2_functional: "Your rules are field orders: few, absolute, and enforced first on your own conduct."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Battle-ready","Disciplined","Surgical"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Pressure":"Pressure is your forge: you harden correctly under loads that crack others. Seek arenas with real stakes. Comfort dulls you faster than any enemy could.","Command":"Command fits you like a sword fits its grip: natural, tested, dangerous if idle. Take charge where the mission deserves it, and practice the harder art, releasing command without losing edge.","Crisis":"In crisis you become simple and effective: triage, decision, stroke. People will remember your calm longer than the emergency. Keep one habit for after: cleaning the blade, debriefing the heart."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 金_正官 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Precise","Incorruptible","Even-handed"],"friction":["Demanding","Unbending","By-the-book"]}
- Sibling cell 金_正官 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your standard admits no rounding. The report is right or it is redone, the table is set correctly or reset, the apology contains the exact words or does not count. Excellence this consistent is genuinely rare, and living beside it is an occupation nobody applied for."

Core element Wood, energy element Metal. Law: Metal tames Wood (金克木: the knife prunes the branch). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Metal is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Wood core that shows Metal on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Metal as the Order is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 木_金's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Being hard on yourself is a rule you never had to learn. Every standard turns into a judge in you, and you fail your own hard test sooner than pass someone else's. Keep in mind that you answer to no judge harder than yourself.

value_b.text: You are harder on yourself than any boss would dare be. Being tested matters more to you than being well, and you grade your week hard instead of living it. Remember that passing your own hard test is permitted.

value.text: The hardness you keep for yourself sets everyone's rate. Your mistakes feel unforgivable, and being hard on people near you comes easier than letting one pass. You take their ease with every mistake your hardness refuses to pass, and it helps to remember that.

value.text: Even on days nothing is asked of you, you stay on duty. Being needed is the only rest you trust, and you pick the next duty rather than the night off. Remind yourself that you are the one keeping you on duty.

value_b.text: Being off duty is the one order you refuse to take. Pressure is the only state you trust, and you stay on duty through a quiet month instead of resting in it. Do not forget that you lost nothing when the duty ended.

value.text: Off duty is a state you never fully manage. The alert in you never stands down, and you spend a free evening on duty rather than inside it. You pay for the duty in rest never taken, a price worth holding on to.

value.text: Pushing too hard is your answer to anything slow. Your own pace is the only safe one, and you push ahead of asking if the push was wanted. Take note that you are using force with every push, whether you mean it kindly or not.

value_b.text: You push too hard because stopping feels more dangerous than pushing. You push yourself first and everyone near you after, since pressure is the one tool you fully trust. You get to set the push down too, and that part is worth keeping.
